messages:
alex.green: quick question — I need to pull a sample of audit logs for a compliance review. Specifically: who has been changing API keys and who impersonated service accounts in the last 30 days. What's the easiest export path (CSV/JSON), and do we have a redaction flag to remove PII (emails, full IPs)?

maria.secops: short answer: yes, you can export both CSV & JSON. default hosted retention is 90d; enterprise customers can configure longer retention/archival. for PII we support redaction transforms on export (email hash, ip truncate). you'll need the audit.export role or an approved access ticket.

alex.green: can you paste a small sample schema/header for CSV? also: can exports be pushed to customer S3 (we need to hand over to a 3rd-party auditor) or is it download-only?

maria.secops: CSV header example (fields we include by default):
```
ts,actor_id,actor_type,actor_display,action,target_id,target_type,target_display,org_id,ip,ip_trunc,location,method,request_path,request_payload_redacted,result,request_id
```
notes: request_payload_redacted will be "true" if payload was redacted. ip_trunc is like 1.2.3.x. email fields are hashed when redact=true.

maria.secops: S3 export: yes — we support pushing exports to a pre-signed customer S3 location for enterprise plans. workflow: create export job -> provide s3 URI + write role -> job uploads chunked gzip CSV/JSON. for hosted free-accounts we provide direct download only.

alex.green: what are the exact permission strings? I need to add them to the infra RBAC doc.

maria.secops: permission bits: "audit.logs.read" (view), "audit.logs.export" (export to download/S3), "audit.logs.admin" (configure retention/archival). service principals need export permission + the s3 write pre-signed URL.

jamal.sre: one gotcha — exports >10GB are split into 1GB gzip parts. our CLI (rctl) will auto-merge locally.

anna.pm: does the export pipeline stripe PII if customer opts-in? we have a customer asking if we can remove email + username from the logs before giving to auditors.

maria.secops: yes — we have 2 modes: 
- redact_on_export: redact email/username/ip in the exported file
- tokenized_on_export: replace PII with consistent pseudonyms (useful for linking events without revealing identity)
Both require an approval ticket in /approvals with reason + expiry. we keep an access log of who requested the export and include that in the export metadata.

sec-bot: Documentation: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/audit-logs#exporting (includes example CLI and S3 steps) :link:  (automated)

alex.green: can you share the rctl example?

maria.secops: sure — example CLI to create a redacted export to S3: 
```bash
rctl audit export \\n  --start 2025-09-01T00:00:00Z \\n  --end 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z \\n  --filter "action:apikey.* OR actor_type:service_account" \\n  --format csv \\n  --redact PII,email,ip \\n  --s3 s3://redwood-audit-uploads/customer-123/2025-09/ \\n  --notify-on-complete alice@company.com
```
(you must have audit.logs.export and an approved export ticket id appended as --approval-id)

jamal.sre: FYI — if you need ad-hoc direct DB queries for deep forensics we require a security review and a short-lived read-only replica role, not a general export.

alex.green: perfect. one more: what's the default retention policy we should call out in the customer-facing page?

maria.secops: default hosted: 90 days. Dedicated/reserved: configurable; typical ent enterprise defaults we set to 365 days and offer archival to cold storage for 7 years on request (legal/compliance customers).

alex.green: thanks — I'll draft the RBAC + product copy. leaving this here in case folks have edits. :thumbsup:

maria.secops: lmk if you want me to add the CSV header snippet to the public docs (we can include an example sample csv).

alex.green: please do, and add the note about required --approval-id & role.

sec-bot: Export job completed (job id: ej-9a2f). uploaded 3 parts to s3://redwood-audit-uploads/customer-123/2025-09/ (automated notification)

alex.green: got it, thanks everyone.
